meta.title: Polish A1
meta.subtitle: 600 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Polish → English (see the Polish, recall the meaning) and English → Polish (see an English meaning, recall the Polish). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 600 words for level A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Poland's State Commission for the Certification of Proficiency in Polish as a Foreign Language examines at all six levels, but no official word list was found for any of them. So 476 of the 600 words were written for Folio, a topic at a time, for the topics the A1 exam is described as covering — people and the family, daily life, free time, the home, places in town, transport and directions, work and school, food, shopping and money, health, the seasons and the weather, and the basic names of plants and animals — together with the numbers, days, months and colours and the pronouns, question words, prepositions and conjunctions every sentence is built from. They are Folio's choice, not the Commission's, and this is not an official word list. The other 124 are the commonest words of everyday Polish not already chosen, from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles, each word counted over all its forms. The cards are ordered by that frequency, so the words met most often come first; the 5 set phrases, which a list of single words cannot count, come last. Polish changes the endings of its nouns, adjectives and verbs, and many stems change with them, so each card carries the forms that cannot be guessed, read from a dictionary rather than generated. 266 nouns show their gender, three cases of the singular and two of the plural — pies: masculine animate, psa, psie, psem, psy, psów. 114 verbs show their aspect and its partner, the forms for ja (I), on (he) and oni (they) and the past of on — iść: imperfective, pójść, idę, idzie, idą, szedł — a perfective verb's being its future, since it has no present. 30 adjectives show their comparative and superlative. 15 personal pronouns show their cases. Real example sentences come with 598 of the 600 words, three apiece for 596, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Meanings, forms and parts of speech: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency ordering: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
